caseno: Death Reference No. 24 of 2001 with Criminal Appeal Nos. 3036 of 2001 and 207 of 2002 and Criminal Jail Appeal No. 2267 of 2001
lawyer:
Md Helaluddin Molla, Deputy Attorney-General with Md Gias Uddin (Mithu), Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the State in all the cases. 
Syed Ziaul Karim with Khair Ahmed, Advocates ----- For the appellants in all the above appeals.
parties:
State ----- Petitioner
Vs
Mir Hossain alias Mira and others ----- Condemned Prisoners
full_judgment:
10. Learned Sessions Judge in awarding conviction and imposing death penalty discussed and considered circumstantial evidence, judicial confessional statements and other materials on record and found: 

 a.	Learned Magistrate after observing all legal formalities recorded confessional statement of accused Khodeja Begum and Mir Hossain alias Mira. Facts revealed in the confessional statements substantially corroborated the prosecution story. Confessing accused did not complain of any torture and ill treatment before making confessional statement. They did not retract their confessional statements. Confessional statements were true and voluntary. Accused Mir Hossain alias Mira and Khodeja Begum could be convicted on the basis of their own statements, although, there were other corroborative evidences. 

 b.	Alamgir remained in abscondence after the occurrence which was very important circumstantial evidence that he was involved in the murder and it reflected his mens rea. There was no earthly reason on his part to remain absconding if he was not a culprit. Accused Alamgir was involved in the murder of Rokeya Begum. 

 c.	All the PWs stated in one voice that accused husband started torturing his first wife deceased Rokeya Begum after his second marriage with Khodeja Begum. Khodeja Begwn in connivance with her husband accused Shah Alam, accused Mir Hossain alias Mira and accused Alamgir killed Rokeya Begwn. Though there was no direct evidence in the case but strong and cogent chain of circumstantial evidence led to the conclusion that none but accused persons in furtherance of common object in collaboration with each other killed Rokeya Begwn. 

 15. Central evidence in proof of guilt of accused persons consisted of testimonies of PW 1 Abdul Gafur, father of deceased Rokeya Begum, PW 2 Abdul Maleque, PW 4 Md Ishaque, PW 5 Md Mahbubul Hoque, PW 6 Ali Akkas, PW 9 Khodeza Akhtar Khanam, PW 10 Md Zasim Uddin Badal and PW 11 Dr ABM Abdul Motaleb. 

 17. PW 2 Abdul Maleque in his evidence stated: Rokeya Begum was given in marriage with accused Shah Alam. Accused Shah Alam subsequently married accused Khodeja Begum. After marriage Shah Alam and Khodeja Begum started torturing Rokeya Begum. Rokeya Begum then left Shah Alam's house and came to her father's house. Accused Shah Alam, thereafter, took Rokeya Begum to his house on the assurance that she would not be tortured. 

 18. PW 4 Md Ishaque, a Union Parishad Member, in his evidence made disclosure: Accused Khodeja Begum and Shah Alam used to torture Rokeya Begum in different manners. 

 19. PW 5 Md Mahbubul Hoque, who is full brother of deceased Rokeya Begum, in his evidence said: At the instigation of accused Khodeja Begum, Shah Alam used to torture his sister. 

 21. PW 9 Khodeza Akhtar Khanam, Magistrate, First Class, recorded the judicial confessional statement of accused Khodeja Begum. It is in her evidence: Confessional statement had been recorded in compliance with rules and procedure of law. Confessional statements were true and voluntary. Accused Khodeja Begum did not mount any allegation to her in respect of any torture upon her. 

 22. PW 10 Md Zasim Uddin Badal, Magistrate, First Class, recorded the judicial confessional statement of accused Mir Hossain alias Mira. His evidence is in the following terms: In compliance with rules and procedures of law judicial confessional statement was recorded. Statement was true and voluntary. 

 II. 	Whether awarding of conviction for offence under sections 302/34 of The Penal Code and imposition of death penalty upon convict-appellants warrants any interference by this Court on evidences, materials on record, fact and circumstances of the case and in safe dispensation of criminal justice. 

 25. The is no eye-witness to commission of murder of Rokeya Begum. Prosecution case rested on circumstantial evidence. Having regarded to manner, place and time of occurrence it was difficult on the part of prosecution to produce any ocular evidence evidencing the commission of murder of deceased Rokeya Begum. It is to be remembered that for a crime to be proved it is not necessary that crime must be seen to have been committed and must in all circumstances be proved by direct ocular evidence by examining before the Court those persons who had witnessed its commission. The principal fact or "factum probandum" may be proved indirectly by means of certain inferences drawn from "factum probans", that is, the probative or evidentiary fact. 

 26. Law relating to circumstantial evidence is well recognised. It requires that prosecution is to prove each of the circumstances having a definite tendency pointing towards guilt of the accused person and, though, each of the circumstances by itself may not be conclusive but the cumulative effect of proved circumstances must be so complete that it would exclude every other hypothesis and unequivocally point to the guilt of the accused. 

 a.	Treatment of condemned prisoner Shah Alam towards deceased Rokeya Begum as evidenced by testimonies of Informant PW 1 Abdul Gafur, PW 2 Abdul Maleque, PW 4 Md Ishaque, PW 5 Md Mahbubul Hoque and PW 6 Ali Akkas: 

 c.	  Evidence of PW 5 Md Mahbubul Hoque to the effect that Belal, son of both convict- appellant Shah Alam and deceased Rokeya Begum made communication with him that convict-appellant Mir Hossain alias Mira called out his mother Rokeya Begum out of the house. 

 e.	Abscondence of convict Alamgir since the incident. Convict Alamgir remained in abscondence till conclusion of trial and he did never submit to the process of court. This act of abscondence on the part of convict Alamgir is a relevant piece of evidence in proof of his guilt and it can be held as a determining link in the chain of circumstantial evidence which must admit of no other reasonable hypothesis than that of guilt of convict Alamgir. 

 f.	 Medico Legal Certificate: Medical evidence of Dr ABM Abdul Motaleb (PW 11) who found one lacerated injury 1½" x 1" just below the left ear, five echymosis of various sizes, 1" x 1½" at the left mendibular region, one lacerated injury ½" x 1" just above the right eye, one echymosis, 2" x 4", in front of the neck and one lacerated injury on the right thumb and death accredited to asphyxia as a result of throttling which was ante-mortem and homicidal in nature. 

 32. Confessional statement having been true and voluntary can form the basis of conviction upon convict-appellant Mir Hossain alias Mira and Khodeja Begum. The maxim "habemus optimum testem canfitentem renum" means confession of accused is the best evidence against him is quite applicable in the case of the convict-appellants Mir Hossain alias Mira and Khodeja Begum. Khodeja Begum in her confessional statement implicated Mir Hossain alias Mira in commission of crime in the terms that Mir Hossain alias Mira called out her Satin (Rokeya Begum) from the house and killed Rokeya Begum. This statement in respect of Mir Hossain alias Mira stands supported by the statement of Mir Hossain alias Mira when he stated that Rokeya Begum had gone to scene of crime. 

 34. Under section 30 of The Evidence Act confession of a co-accused can be taken into consideration and on the strength of that confession another co-accused can be convicted provided the said confession is corroborated by any other evidence, either direct and circumstantial. 

 35. Section 30 of The Evidence Act enjoins that when more persons than one are being tried jointly for the same offence, and a confession made by one of such persons affecting himself and some other of such persons is proved, the Court may take into consideration such confession as against such persons as well as against the person who makes such confession. 

 36. It is true that confession of a co-accused does not come within the definition of evidence embodied in section 3 of The Evidence Act and obviously an evidence of a very weak type but court can consider, act and use confession of a co-accused to base conviction upon another co-accused. From confession of convict-appellant Mir Hossain alias Mira it came to light that Alamgir had a dagger in his hand and he stabbed with dagger. It, also, came out from confessional statement of Khodeja Begum that Alamgir along with Mir Hossain alias Mira killed Rokeya Begum. Convict Alamgir absconded immediately after the incident and this is a circumstance which is considered sufficient corroboration of the confessional statement of convict-appellant Mir Hossain alias Mira and Khodeja Begum. Abscondence of convict Alamgir furnished a strong corroboration of confessional statement of Mir Hossain alias Mira and Khodeja Begum. 

 37. We now turn to convict-appellant Shah Alam who is no other than the husband of deceased Rokeya Begum. Four children were born of the wedlock of convict-appellant Shah Alam and deceased Rokeya Begum. Admittedly, Rokeya Begum had been in the house of Shah Alam prior to incident. It came out from confessional statement of convict-appellant Mir Hossain alias Mira that he called out Rokeya Begum from the house and took her to the scene of crime. It came out from testimonies of PWs 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 that after marriage with Khodeja Begum, Shah Alam and Khodeja Begum used to torture and assault Rokeya Begum. Evidences of PWs 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 in respect of torture and assault upon Rokeya Begum, silence and inaction on the part of convict-appellant Shah Alam in not setting the criminal law in motion and, also, the judicial confessional statement of convict-appellant Mir Hossain alias Mira and other tell-tale circumstances unerringly point towards the guilt of convict-appellant Shah Alam in the crime. 

 42. Commission of crime and criminal sharing of overt act on the part of the convict-appellants and their presence at the scene of crime had been proved by judicial confessional statements which stood supported by other circumstantial evidences and, also, some other circumstances and taking into stock the laws and principles of common intention engrafted in section 34 of The Penal Code and, also, culpable homicide amounting to murder punishable under section 302 of The Penal Code the inevitable conclusion that flows is that a meeting of minds and a fusion of ideas took place amongst the convict-appellants and in prosecution of act of convict- appellants flowed out as if in obedience to the command of a single mind. Convict-appellants seem to have been rightly charged and convicted for offence of section 302 read with section 34 of The Penal Code.
